magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A raven, snake or negro dressed in black. It makes the wearer angry, bold, courageous and a backbiter, gives bad dreams, the power of summon- ing or driving away evil spirits and protection from winds and the malice of men and devils.

magic_fixed_stars.name: Antares
magic_fixed_stars.rules: Sardonyx, amethyst, long aristotochy and saffron, * -
magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A man armed with a coat of mail, or a scorpion. It gives understanding and memory, help against evil spirits, and the power of driving them away and binding them.

magic_fixed_stars.name: Arcturus
magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A horse, wolf, or man dancing. It cures fevers, retains the blood and acts' as an astring- ent.

magic_fixed_stars.name: Capella
magic_fixed_stars.rules: ' Sapphire, horebound, mint, mugwort and mandrake
magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A man playing musical instruments. It makes the wearer -honoured and exalted before nobility and cures the toothache.

magic_fixed_stars.name: Deneb Algedi
magic_fixed_stars.rules: Chalcedony, marjoram, mugwort, nip and mandrake root
magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A hart, goat, or angry man. It gives prosperity and increased wrath.

magic_fixed_stars.name: Pleiades
magic_fixed_stars.rules: Crystal and the stone Diodocus, the herb Diacedon, frankincense, fennel and quicksilver
magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A little virgin or a lamp. It strengthens the eyesight, assembles spirits, raises winds and reveals secret and hidden things.

magic_fixed_stars.name: Polaris
magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A pensive man, a bull, or a calf. It protects against spells- and renders the wearer secure in travel.

magic_fixed_stars.name: pROCYON
magic_fixed_stars.rules: The stone Achates/ flowers of marigold, pennyroyal
magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A cock, or three little maids. It gives the favour of gods, spirits and men, power against witchcraft, and preserves the health.

magic_fixed_stars.name: Regulus
magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A lion, cat, or an honourable person seated in a chair. It makes the wearer temperate, gives favour and appeases wrath.

magic_fixed_stars.name: Sirius
magic_fixed_stars.rules: Beryl, savine, mugwort, dragonwort and the tongue of a snake
magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A hound or a little virgin. It gives honour, the goodwill and favour of men and the airy spirits, and the power to pacify nobles and others.

magic_fixed_stars.name: Spica
magic_fixed_stars.rules: Emerald, sage, trefoil, periwinkle i mug- wort and mandrake
magic_fixed_stars.image_effect: A bird, or a man laden with merchandise. It gives riches, overcomes contentions, and removes scarcity and mischief.

No account of the astrological influences ascribed to the fixed stars would be complete without some mention of their effect upon the weather. In the 17th century astro-meteorology occupied a prominent position and received a great deal of attention, but at the present time it has apparently ceased to in- terest any but the almanac maker, and its modern followers mostly practise the slipshod and almost useless method of noting the daily aspects in the ephemeris and predicting from those alone.

In the old days it was customary to base the major ■weather predictions upon the positions of the planets in the horoscopes for the entry of the Sun info the four cardinal signs Aries, Cancer, Libra and Capricorn, together with those for great conjunctions and eclipses. These general indications were then am- plified by a. study oi New AIooos, FuU Moons, Quarter Lunations and in some cases daily horo- scopes.

It is no part of my present plan to describe the methods and rules at length, but merely to draw attention to the fact that in the following account of stellar influences the positions are understood to be those occurring at significant epochs, such as

The general type of effect appears to follow the nature of the star. Thus the Sun being with Satur nian stars is said to indicate cold, rain or snow ; with Jupitcrian stars, a serene and temperate air ; with Martial stars, thunder-storms ; with Venusian stars, rain, moisture and mist; and, with Mercurial stars, wind. Much importance was attached to the rising and setting of stars, especially in their re- lationship to the Sun, and it is a well-known fact that the ancient Egyptians began their New Year at the time when Sirius rose with the Sun at the Summer Solstice and marked the beginning of the inundations. All the ways in which a star could rise or set with the Sun were carefully classified in very early times and given distinctive names, but only two need concern us here, namely, Mainline and Vespertine, the former of which is applied to a star that rises and sets before the Sun, and the latter to one that rises and sets after it.

In addition to the individual star influences, the lunar mansion in which a lunation, ingress or con- junction fell was held to affect the weather in ac- cordance with its nature. The meteorological na- ture of each of the Arabic mansions has been handed down to us, and, beginning with A1 Thurayya, is as follows : r.
